simple.meaning: תְּנוּבָה (tᵉnûwbâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “produce.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 32:13. The surrounding context includes death, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּנוּבָה (H8570) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H8570. tenubah תְּנוּבָה noun feminine fruit, produce ; — absolute Isa 27:6 ; construct תְּנוּבֵת Ezek 36:30 ; תְּנוּבָתִי Judg 9:11 ; plural תְּנוּבֹת Deut 32:13 , וֺת - Lam 4:9 ; especially ׳ת שָׂדַי fruit, produce, of field Deut 32:13 ; Lam 4:9 ; compare ׳ת הַשָּׂדֶה Ezek 36:30 (|| העץ פרי ); of fig-tree Judg 9:11 ; metaphor of Israel ת ׳פְנֵיתֵֿבֵל וּמָֽלְאוּ Isa 27:6 (|| ישׂ ופרח יציץ יעקב ׳יַשְׁרֵשׁ ).

occurrences.englishText: He made him ride on the high places of the earth.
“But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. They will fill the surface of the world with fruit.
Those who are killed with the sword are better than those who are killed with hunger;
I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field, that you may receive no more the reproach of famine among the nations.
